A1.justification: Both readable, complete 11-page PDFs describe the same IAPL study, with corresponding methods, equations, five figures and nine tables. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix, despite v3's references to supplementary material.

before.justification: v3 reports original IAPL results on UniversalFakeDetect and GenImage, component and sensitivity ablations in Tables 4–9, and visual analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains the original benchmark results, ablations and visual analyses reported in v3.

M1.justification: The adapters, learnable tokens, conditional feature extractors, test-time entropy tuning and optimal input selection are unchanged. Explicitly writing the sum of the existing training losses clarifies their combination without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same AI-generated image detection task on UniversalFakeDetect and GenImage, with the same generator subsets and test scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain identical comparator membership within each experiment, including MiraGe and ATTSD where previously evaluated. The newly cited related works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The ProGAN and SDv1.4 training settings, evaluation metrics, accuracy threshold, CLIP backbone, training budget and test-time tuning settings remain unchanged in Sections 4.1–4.2 and the table captions.

E4.justification: Tables 4–9 retain the same component, adapter-placement, token-layer, entropy-loss and tuning-step analyses. The t-SNE and Grad-CAM analyses in Figures 2 and 5 are also retained; removing supplementary pointers does not establish removal of experiments from the supplied PDFs.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–9 match. IAPL retains 95.61% mAcc and 99.32% mAP on UniversalFakeDetect and 96.7% mAcc on GenImage; the qualitative result panels also retain the same content.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 and the mathematical reasoning are unchanged. The new inline training-loss sum formalizes the previously described two-loss combination rather than introducing a new theoretical result or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same adaptive-prompt, generalization and state-of-the-art performance claims. The conclusion replaces its explicit superiority sentence with generic performance wording, but the paper's substantive claim scope remains unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning instance adaptation, prediction consistency, forgery localization and efficiency–performance trade-offs remain unchanged. No substantive limitations or applicability qualifications are added or removed.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 now explicitly specifies Loverall = Lcls + Laux, clarifying the unweighted combination previously described only in prose. Hyperparameters, hardware and the code link are unchanged; supplementary pointers are removed without supplying additional CNN architecture details.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds citations to Beyond Artifacts, MIRROR, and Scaling Up AI-Generated Image Detection with Generator-Aware Prototypes. These modestly expand the existing foundation-model discussion without changing IAPL's positioning or adding substantive comparisons.

P1.justification: v4 revises affiliations, adds acknowledgments, clarifies the loss paragraph, shortens the conclusion, removes supplementary pointers and corrects bibliographic entries. Most prose and the section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Several schematics and the Grad-CAM panel are slightly reduced or repositioned, with accompanying text reflow and table-highlight formatting adjustments. The same five figures and nine tables remain, without substantive display-content changes.

improvement.justification: The explicit loss combination in Section 3.3 modestly improves reproducibility, while corrected references and added related-work citations improve documentation. The scientific evidence is unchanged, and removing supplementary pointers does not resolve the missing detailed CNN architecture description, so the overall gain is limited.
